content.text:
Yes, two things in `01_samplesheets/rnaseq_bulk_design.csv` and `00_data/rnaseq_bulk/files.csv` bear on how you read a control vs treated test.

**1. Lane is partly confounded with condition.** Each sample was sequenced on a single lane, and the lanes don't split evenly across the groups:

| Lane | control | treated |
|---|---|---|
| L001 | S2 | S4, S5 |
| L002 | S1, S3 | S6 |

Control is 2 on L002 and 1 on L001, and treated is the reverse. The confounding is partial, not complete, so the design isn't unusable. A lane effect would still be partly mixed into the condition effect, though. That matters most if the two lanes were different runs or flowcells. If they were two lanes of the same flowcell, lane effects are usually small.

The samplesheet and design table carry no batch or lane column. Stage 02 asks for a `formula`, and `lane` isn't a column in `design.csv`, so the formula can't adjust for it as the design stands. Whether the lanes share a flowcell isn't recorded in anything I'm allowed to read at this stage.

**2. There are only 3 replicates per group.** That is enough for a test (the stage 01 check requires at least 2 per group). Power is limited, though, so only large effects will be reliably detected. The dispersion estimates will also lean heavily on shrinkage, and a single outlier sample would have a large influence.

Both are about the design and the data, not about whether the samplesheet is well formed. The samplesheet itself validated cleanly: 6 of 6 samples, paired-end, and sample IDs and conditions that match.

If you want lane handled differently, say so before approving. Adding a column to the design is your edit to make, and I won't make it. Otherwise, say when you're ready and I'll start stage 02.
